vulnerabilities.description: Weak random ID generation in fallback path. The idFactory fallback uses Math.random().toString(16).slice(2, 10) instead of cryptographically secure randomness. While crypto.randomUUID() is preferred, the fallback should use a secure alternative or fail safely.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove the Math.random() fallback or use a proper CSPRNG. If crypto.randomUUID() is unavailable, throw an error or use the browser's crypto.getRandomValues().

vulnerabilities.description: Token injection via window object globals (TOKEN, PORT). While guards exist, injecting security-sensitive values as window properties creates an XSS attack surface. If page scripts are compromised, tokens can be exfiltrated.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use postMessage() with strict origin checking instead of window globals. Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent script injection. Consider using sessionStorage with HTTPOnly flag if available.

vulnerabilities.description: Unvalidated JSON.parse() of stored session data. Malformed or malicious session data in localStorage could cause crashes or unexpected behavior. No schema validation before use.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add schema validation using a parsing library (e.g., zod, valibot). Validate that parsed.checkpointRevision is a number before using it.

vulnerabilities.description: CSS escape function relies on String.replace() fallback when CSS.escape is unavailable. This may not handle all CSS injection vectors (e.g., unicode escapes, property names).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use a tested CSS sanitization library or ensure CSS.escape() is always available via polyfill. Add unit tests for CSS injection payloads.

vulnerabilities.description: Session state stored in unencrypted localStorage. XSS attacks or browser storage inspection can expose session IDs and application state.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Encrypt sensitive session data before storing. Use sessionStorage for ephemeral data. Implement automatic session expiration. Consider using IndexedDB with encryption for large state.

vulnerabilities.description: Double-init guard checks window.__IMPECCABLE_LIVE_INIT__ but doesn't validate the guard itself. A malicious script could set this flag to prevent legitimate initialization or set it falsely to enable re-execution.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use Symbol or Object.defineProperty() with non-configurable flag to make guard tamper-resistant: Object.defineProperty(window, '__IMPECCABLE_LIVE_INIT__', { value: true, writable: false }).
